chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Malik al-Juhani, from Abdullah ibn Ata'a, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and saw in his house rugs, pillows, patterns (carpets/rugs), and amenities (furnishings). So I said, 'What is this?' He said, 'The belongings of the wife.'

key_terms.أَنْمَاطاً: Patterns, often referring to decorated carpets or rugs
key_terms.بُسُطاً: Rugs or carpets spread on the floor
key_terms.مَتَاعُ الْمَرْأَةِ: The belongings or possessions of the wife
key_terms.مَرَافِقَ: Amenities or furnishings used for sitting and living

ai.seo_question: What are considered the personal belongings of a wife in Shia Islamic tradition according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s appreciation for domestic comfort and aesthetic order, countering ascetic extremes by validating the beauty of household items like carpets and cushions. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the home is a space of dignity and tranquility, where the wife’s personal belongings are respected as part of the family’s shared heritage. The scene reflects the practical application of *adab* (etiquette) within the marital sphere, emphasizing harmony and mutual respect.
